tested:
── Huawei CloudEngine (Wave 21 U2, NPX-820) ─────────────────────────────
Built from a LIVE BOOT, not from a template: EVE-NG ships no CloudEngine template at
all (its only Huawei ones are huaweiar1k / huaweine40 / huaweiusg6kv), so rule #33's
"pull the real template first" has nothing to pull and rule #22 forbids guessing the
rest. Everything below is what actually booted on this host 2026-09-05.
Probe argv, mirroring raw_qemu.py's own construction: -machine pc -cpu host -m 4096
-smp 2, virtio disk (the shipped file is virtioa.qcow2), 4 x e1000 NICs, system QEMU
10.2.1. Both images then ran their platform bring-up to completion and dropped to a
real VRP prompt on the first serial port:
[01:23:35] Step01: CHK-USERRIGHT .....Finish   ...   Step07: CHK-SVR ......Finish
[01:24:55] Step08: START-BOARD ........Finish   [01:24:55] Step09: START-ROUTER ...Finish
<HUAWEI>
VRP (R) software, Version 8.180 (CE6800 V200R005C10SPC607B607)
~80 s from the first bring-up step to the prompt on an idle-ish host; boot_timeout_sec
is set to 300 to leave real headroom on this shared box rather than to describe a
best case.
THE NIC COUNT IS A BOOT REQUIREMENT, not a preference (root-caused from the guest's
own log, not inferred): with a single NIC the bring-up fails at
Step06: CHK-MULTICAST ....Error   Step07: START-ROUTER ....Error   reason=246
and drops to the underlying Debian shell (root@debian:/opt/svrp#) instead of VRP. The
guest's /opt/svrp/start_svrp.sh line 789 logs "addMutiCastRoute: route add 225.1.0.1
dev eth1 failed, reason code=7" - it hard-codes eth1, so the VM must have at least
TWO interfaces. Re-run with 4 NICs, both images reached <HUAWEI> first try. A node
drawn from the palette gets 4 NICs, and Wave 21's own harness creates 2, so this
holds on both real paths; the general "a vendor can require a minimum NIC count and
nothing enforces it" gap is NPX-154 (already logged against vwlc for the same
reason) and is not re-fixed here.
Interface names come from the running device's own configuration, not from docs:
MEth0/0/0 is management and GE1/0/0.. are data ports on BOTH images (see MGMT_INFO
and DATA_IFACE_NAMING below). CLI verbs live in node-manager's VENDOR_CLI["huawei"],
which carries its own console transcript.
